name: targeted-1026-202436
hypothesis: Most costly pattern: missed first promotions. At a half-year review, Skill, Network or Output sits just below the high it had already reached at that level, because a story chosen after the last quarterly phase pulled it down; between that phase and the review only stories move these three. Both early exits (ladd-00001 and scre-00004, the champion's only exits, both dismissed for capability at the fourth review) missed their first three reviews this way. ladd-00001 lost Output at the first review (two stories just before it cost 3 Output: a health-for-delivery swap at Health 5 and an optional cross-team reading load, taken because Network looked weakest although it had stopped rising), Skill and Network at the second, and Output at the third. scre-00004 lost Output at the first (an optional formal thank-you note) and at the second (a health-for-delivery swap at Health 7), then Network at the third (a hands-off mentoring choice, together with a risk-driven D); its promotion at the fourth review came too late to stop the dismissal. Across all 6 digests, 20 reviews were held at the first two levels. In all 11 without a promotion, one of the three had stood at its level high after the last quarterly phase and stories pulled it below that before the review. In the 8 promotions whose state is visible, all three stood at their highs, 3 of them only because a story had just won back a Network dip. The same slips cost completed careers levels: scre-00002 lost its first review to three Output-costing stories, and ladd-00003 lost three of its five reviews at the first two levels and reached the third level a year late. In those 11 review windows, 11 of the 15 Output drops came from side work or putting off one's own work, and 11 of the 13 Network drops from correcting or refusing someone (the other 2 from reporting a colleague). The parent's story rule protects only Health and Dignity and says to help the weakest, so the player traded Output for rest at mid Health, or for Network that could not rise. Lessons G4 shows why this decides survival: games first promoted at the first or second review completed 19 of 25, later ones 0 of 13. The change makes Skill, Network and Output protected in every story, ranked below the honesty and risk rules, and adds a repair step after any dip. That keeps all three at their highs on review day, which every visible promotion needed. First promotions should then come at the first or second review, capability dismissals should fall, and completed careers should gain level and salary.
change: Inserted one priority between Review and Balance, the promotion guard: in every story, Skill, Network and Output count as protected because each half-year review decides promotion on them as they stand that day. Among the options the earlier rules allow, keep all three; give one up for rest only when Health or Dignity is in the lower part of its range, never for side work or a gain elsewhere, and win back any dip with the next choices. One sentence says which kinds of option usually cost Output or Network. Everything else is the parent's text word for word (Balance is renumbered and the description extended). 494 words by wc -w, against the parent's 393.
predicted_behaviour: Story notes cite the guard alongside the signal state. With Health and Dignity outside the lower part of their range, the player turns down side work (extra reviews, formal write-ups, learning bets) and swaps that put off its own work, whenever an honest alternative exists. After a story lowers Skill, Network or Output, the next notes name the dip and the next choice aims to win it back. At reviews held at the first two levels, the three stand at their highs more often. The first promotion comes at the first or second review in nearly every game (parent digests: 4 of 6, plus one at the fourth review and one never), and the second promotion follows sooner. Capability dismissals fall from the parent's 2 in 12, and completion is at least 10 of 12. Completed games end with a level dimension above the parent's 46 and wealth above its 33. Risk control stays near 74, with still no trust crises or blackouts. Energy, main actions and risk handling look like the parent's.
refutation: Refuted if, with the same actor, any of these holds: capability dismissals are not fewer than the parent's 2 in 12; the share of games first promoted at the first or second review does not rise above the parent's; completed games do not end with a level dimension above 46. Refuted as harmful if trust crises or blackouts appear (none in the parent's 12) or risk control falls clearly below 74; that would mean the guard pushed the player to narrow disclosures or to overwork. Manipulation check: the text was not executed, and the result says nothing about the idea, if story notes never mention keeping Skill, Network and Output, or if side work and swaps that put off the player's own work are still taken at comfortable Health in the stories before a review.
